Geometric Social

Note on how outcome was derive:

  1. Remove frames coded as “nobabyface”, “noface”, “none”, or “away”

  2. Remove “left”, “right” frames with confidence < 85%

  3. Use “left” vs “right” to code “target” vs “non-target” depending on the task and version. Calculate % looking for each social side as:

    % looking = (target) / (target + non-target)

    *left & right frames all need to have >= 85% confidence. A trial must have at least 33% usable data (i.e. left, right frames at 85% confidence) to be included.

Prediction

2 versions LthenR vs RthenL

Note on how outcome was derive:

  1. Remove frames coded as “nobabyface”, “noface”, “none”, or “away”
  2. Remove “left”, “right” frames with confidence < 85%
  3. Use “left” vs “right” to code “target” vs “non-target” depending on the task and version. For each test trials for each block (2-8) and (10-16), an AEM = if participant looks at target at all during critical window.

For each block, compute total trials per participant, then calculate proportion of AEM trials as final outcome.

Analysis

Word recognition

How outcome was derived:

Example of foot and milk (paired).

The word foot is the target in trial 1 and the distractor at trial 9. the difference for foot = % looking at the word foot in trial 1 - % looking at the word foot in trial 9. Simplified:

foot_diff = trial1_target - trial9_distractor = trial1_target - (1 - trial9_target) = trial1_target + trial9_target - 1

But remember that the words are paired (these pairs are always shown together): foot ~ milk banana ~ hair hand ~ yogurt eyes ~ cookie mouth ~ apple

The word milk then the target at trial 9 but the distractor at trial 1. So then for “milk”: the difference for milk = % looking at the word milk in trial 9 - % looking at the word milk in trial 1. Simplified:

milk_diff = trial9_target – trial1_distractor = trial9_target - (1 - trial1_target) = trial9_target + trial1_target - 1

And then if you look at the math, foot_diff comes out to be the same as milk_diff (trial1_target + trial9_target – 1), so we just use this word-paired data once & we have 5 pairs in total. Kiddos will have up to 5 rows of final difference score.

The same thing repeats for trial 11 and trial 19.

Then the final data for foot ~ milk is: average %target - average %distractor = average of trial1_target & trial11_target - average of trial9_distractor & trial19_distractor.
